subject: Usage flattening & cost-smoothing playbook
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 14 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Usage flattening & cost-smoothing playbook

Hi Sanjay / Olivia,

TL;DR: Q3 token spend spiked during the launch window and has since flattened ~35% below peak. We've modeled three renewal options that smooth cost while preserving headroom for weekly surges — attached is the CSV export and a compact playbook PDF.

What we saw:
- Production inference tokens peaked at ~1.8M/day during the first two weeks of the campaign.
- Peak was driven by a combination of higher per-session length (15% longer avg prompt) and a temporary retrain rollout that increased assistant verbosity.
- Over the last 30 days usage has normalized to ~950k tokens/day (≈47% of peak).

What we recommend (summary):
1) Convert the short-term surge strategy into a 20% uplift on committed baseline (reduces unit price immediately).
2) Add a 1-month burst credit bucket (flex) sized for the 95th percentile daily peak to avoid overage noise in billing months.
3) Apply conservative batching & prefix caching on the top-5 high-traffic routes (we estimate ~12% token reduction in steady-state).

Business impact (conservative):
- Net unit cost reduction of ~18% vs current pay-as-you-go in months where commit covers >80% of traffic.
- Estimated monthly savings (after commit amortization): $8.6k — $12.4k depending on traffic mix.

Attachments: clearmap_q3_token_mix.csv (raw counts), redwood_capacity_playbook_v2.pdf (pricing tables + rollout steps).

Can we get 30 minutes next week to walk the numbers with your procurement and infra leads? Jordan — can you coordinate availability and bring the updated commitment pricing (v2)?

Thanks,
Marissa

Marissa — thanks for the clean write-up and the model. A couple of quick clarifying questions before we lock a meeting:

1) Latency sensitivity: you mention batching and prefix caching. Can you quantify expected p50/p95 latency delta for our top-5 routes? Our product team is worried about user-visible latency increases if batching is too aggressive.

2) Commit sizing: the 20% uplift — is that measured against our current run-rate (950k/day) or versus peak? We need the proposal to be defensible to our finance lead.

3) ROI math: interested in the amortization assumptions. The $8.6k – $12.4k range is broad — can you include a conservative/case/best table?

We can do a 30-min sync on Wed 20th at 10:00 PT if that works for you and Jordan. Procurement will also want a plain English note of how burst credits interact with month-end trueups.

Subject: Re: Usage flattening & cost-smoothing playbook (numbers + latency expectations)

Sanjay / Olivia — thanks for the questions. Short answers first, then the attachment summary.

1) Latency (p50/p95): with the conservative batching profile we've modeled (batch windows tuned to 50–70ms), p50 is effectively unchanged and p95 increases by ~18–25ms on the heavy routes. If low-latency routes are flagged we leave them on single-request paths; the playbook calls out top-2 low-latency flows to exclude from batching.

2) Commit sizing: the 20% uplift is against your current normalized run-rate (950k/day). We also include an alternate bucket measured vs peak (the proposal PDF labels that as "peak-buffer option").

3) ROI table: attached to the PDF — three scenarios (conservative / expected / aggressive) with assumptions annotated. Conservative assumes only 8% token reduction from caching; expected assumes 12%; aggressive assumes 18%.

Key operational notes:
- Burst credits: paid as part of the commitment but only consumed when daily usage > committed baseline. Unused burst in month does not roll forward. We can set a true-up policy to convert residual burst usage into credit for the following month (one-time, on renewal).
- Canary plan: we propose a 2-week canary with traffic split 5% then 15% before full scale to validate latency and cache hit improvements.

I attached the redwood_capacity_playbook_v2.pdf which includes the price table, a 12-month amortization view, and an explicit procurement-ready paragraph for your finance team. Also attached the raw clearmap_q3_token_mix.csv for your engineers.

If Wed 20th 10:00 PT still works, Jordan — please send an invite and include procurement and infra. If not, propose two alternate slots.

Best,
Marissa

Thanks all — quick recap and ops items from today's sync: 

Recap:
- ClearMap signs up for the 20% baseline uplift (committed) plus a 1-month burst bucket sized at the 95th percentile observed peak; we landed on a 1.2M tokens/day committed baseline for month 1, ramping to 1.14M/day as we apply caching and batching.
- Canary plan approved: 2-week rollout (5% -> 15% -> full) with p95 SLIs instrumented and a rollback threshold at +50ms delta.
- Procurement asks for a single-page procurement statement and a DocuSign-ready quote; Marissa uploaded the recommended wording to Drive and the DocuSign draft link is below.
